verdicts.text: Proposals for project TR202504 must be submitted to MoDOTResearchRFP@modot.mo.gov by August 21, 2024 at 10 a.m. Central.
The submittal must include a project plan.
The Offeror must respond to the RFP within the stated submission deadlines, as time is of the essence.
The Offeror must agree to provide the services at the fees quoted, under the terms of this RFP.
The proposal must be signed by an authorized signatory of the Offeror and dated.
The proposal must include the Offeror's printed or typed name, mailing address, city, state, zip, telephone, fax and electronic mail address.
The bidder must be a qualified organization able to conduct the TR202504 "Using AI/ML to Write Legal Land Descriptions" study for the MHTC and Missouri Department of Transportation (MoDOT).
Property descriptions prepared on behalf of the MHTC must be prepared in a manner that meets the requirements outlined in the MoDOT Engineering Policy Guide (EPG) Section 236.4.6.2.
Realty rights acquired or conveyed by the MHTC must be described using the metes and bounds method, unless the property is acquired in its entirety.
When a property is acquired in its entirety, the property description must be written exactly as it appears on the last deed of record for the subject property.
The property description must recite the specific rights being acquired, conveyed or leased when those rights are less than fee simple title.
The AI/ML solution must produce a "first draft" of the legal land description (LLD) using the MHTC parameters, which MoDOT's Right of Way staff can then review and edit.
The contract period will run for 15 months.
All RFP events must occur between 7:30 a.m. and 4 p.m. Central time.
Email to MoDOTResearchRFP@modot.mo.gov is the only acceptable method of contact regarding the RFP, and contacting MoDOT employees by other methods is prohibited and is cause for disqualification.
Questions and comments must be submitted no later than 7/17/2024 at 4 p.m. Central.
A proposal is not considered submitted until the submitter receives notification of receipt from MoDOT.
The Offeror must demonstrate the AI writing a legal land description.
Proposals must include a work plan with a proposed timeline.
Quarterly updates must be submitted electronically to the MoDOT project manager.
An interim presentation must be scheduled near the mid-point of the project to update MoDOT on progress and project direction.
E-mail and phone communications with MoDOT contacts are required throughout the project to provide ongoing progress updates.
The final invoice is due and the contract ends on 2/2/2026.

component_records.title: Bid submission and RFP clarification discipline
component_records.description: We respond to the RFP within the stated submission deadlines, treating time as of the essence: the proposal is filed to MoDOTResearchRFP@modot.mo.gov before the 8/21/2024 10 a.m. Central deadline, in the required single combined PDF, and we do not treat it as submitted until MoDOT's notification of receipt arrives. All questions and comments are submitted to MoDOTResearchRFP@modot.mo.gov no later than 7/17/2024 at 4 p.m. Central, and no MoDOT employee is contacted by any other method, since that is cause for disqualification. We diarise the 7/31/2024 posting of MoDOT's public responses and the 9/18/2024 selection or interview notification, and we hold the proposal complete and unambiguous as submitted because MHTC may accept it without further clarification. This component also carries the bid-stage compliance paperwork: the signed Proposal Submission Form, the Price Page cost estimate, the E-Verify affidavit and, for a sole proprietorship or partnership, the Exhibit B lawful-presence affidavit sworn before a notary.

component_records.title: Project management, governance and MoDOT coordination
component_records.description: A named project manager runs the study for MHTC through the Research Unit of the Construction and Materials Division, with Research Director Jen Harper as MHTC's representative. We facilitate a kick-off meeting to review the work plan, scope and schedule and to establish the protocol for regular ongoing communications and coordination with the team, and we schedule and conduct quarterly project status meetings that review progress for the previous period and anticipated work for the next. Minutes are developed for the kick-off meeting and for every quarterly status meeting and circulated to MoDOT. E-mail and phone communications with MoDOT contacts run throughout the project to give ongoing progress updates, and we fully coordinate our activities with those of the Construction and Materials Division, making advice and information on matters covered by the Agreement available to that Division for the whole effective period. We consult MHTC's representative on any concern arising in the administration of the services, and the project plan expressly recognises MoDOT's ultimate authority to approve work plans. The plan is built to the 15-month contract period with the final invoice due and the contract ending 2/2/2026, and all RFP events are scheduled within 7:30 a.m. to 4 p.m. Central time.

component_records.title: Work plan, schedule and cost estimate
component_records.description: We submit a work plan of no more than ten pages that covers every item in Section 2 of the RFP, sets out the proposed timeline against the RFP milestone dates, and states MoDOT's authority to approve it. The cost estimate covers all services in the Scope of Work, is presented on Section (4), Price Page, of the proposal, and is broken out by Salaries, Benefits, Operating Expense, Facilities and Administration (F&A) Cost and Miscellaneous with a Total, with every Miscellaneous item itemised on an attached sheet. Pricing is held within the $175,000 not-to-exceed amount and we agree to provide the services at the fees quoted under the terms of the RFP. The plan sequences the literature review, program naming and IS approval, proof of concept, training and reporting so that each RFP milestone date is met.

component_records.title: Data Management Plan and data handling
component_records.description: Within two weeks after the kick-off meeting we submit a Data Management Plan that describes the anticipated format or formats our data and related files will use, and that commits to platform-independent, non-proprietary formats so the training corpus of previously approved and filed legal land descriptions and the resulting outputs retain maximum future utility for MoDOT. The plan also sets out how MHTC-supplied descriptions are stored, versioned and separated from derived working files, and how the corpus is retired or handed over at contract end.

component_records.title: Literature search and review of state DOT practice
component_records.description: We conduct a thorough literature search and review of other state DOT practices using AI/ML for right-of-way purposes, covering peer-reviewed research, DOT research reports and published agency guidance, and we summarise what each source implies for MoDOT's EPG Section 236.4.6.2 drafting rules. Findings are delivered as a written review chapter that feeds the Synthesis Report and the final report, and they inform the choice of program named for approval and the design of the proof of concept.

component_records.title: Program selection and MoDOT Information Systems approval
component_records.description: Before any proof-of-concept work begins we name the program we will use to develop the LLDs, together with the version, licensing position, hosting model and security documentation MoDOT Information Systems needs to review it, and we do not proceed to Task 3c until MoDOT Information Systems has approved it. The named program is selected to sit inside the approved technology envelope — .NET 6.0 or above (or a currently supported .NET Framework 4.8 or above where specifically needed), MVC, Razor Pages or Web API, and C#, JavaScript, CSS, HTML or Python — so that approval is not delayed by a stack exception. Any third-party tool or library that would place a licensing responsibility on MoDOT is put to the Information Systems Best Practices Review Team (BRPT) and IS management for prior review and approval, and Python is confined to ESRI scripts and small one-time uses unless BRPT approves larger-scale use.

component_records.title: AI/ML legal land description drafting engine
component_records.description: We build the drafting engine that produces a first draft legal land description from MHTC parameters for MoDOT Right of Way staff to review and edit, with the review-and-edit step designed into the workflow rather than bolted on. The engine encodes MoDOT Engineering Policy Guide (EPG) Section 236.4.6.2 so that drafts follow the required form: metes and bounds descriptions for realty rights acquired or conveyed, except where a property is acquired in its entirety, in which case the description is reproduced exactly as it appears on the last deed of record. Where less than fee simple title is conveyed, the draft recites the specific rights being acquired, conveyed or leased, and parcels are described by metes and bounds, lot calls or 1/4 - 1/4 calls as the source records allow. Every draft carries a surveyor review flag so that a professional land surveyor verifies the parcel against the right-of-way plans and the gathered survey information before any deed is presented to a grantor. The application is a web-based browser application requiring no client-side software beyond a modern browser, built on .NET 6.0 or above with MVC, Razor Pages or Web API in C# and JavaScript, tested against the latest IS-approved browsers, with library dependencies reviewed and updated annually.

component_records.title: Proof-of-concept demonstration on a range of properties
component_records.description: We demonstrate how the technology creates draft legal land descriptions for a variety of properties, using the corpus of previously approved and filed descriptions MoDOT supplies for training and a set of held-out parcels spanning different acquisition types, including whole-property acquisitions and partial takings with less than fee simple rights. The demonstration is run live at the 4/25/2025 milestone so MoDOT staff can see the AI writing a legal land description, and MoDOT's review comments are captured as structured improvement feedback that drives the adjustment cycle before the manual and training are produced. We also present progress and direction at the interim presentation near the project mid-point, scheduled 9/15/2025, so MoDOT can decide whether mid-project corrections are necessary.

component_records.title: ROW staff training and user manual
component_records.description: Once the system is developed and finalised we train MoDOT Right of Way staff on its use, delivering a hands-on session built around the actual drafting workflow — parameter entry, draft generation, review and edit, and surveyor verification — with the adjusted system in place by the 7/25/2025 milestone. The training is supported by a user manual that staff keep as a reference, covering each screen, the EPG Section 236.4.6.2 rules the engine applies, and the escalation path when a draft needs surveyor correction. Both the training and the manual are delivered in accessible formats consistent with WCAG 2.1 AA so that staff using assistive technology can use them.

component_records.title: Synthesis Report, final report and research summary
component_records.description: We prepare a draft Synthesis Report and Research Summary, together with the accompanying documentation identified as beneficial during the study, as final products except for revisions based on MoDOT's review, and we deliver them on 11/3/2025. The final report details every task completed during the project and all findings generated over its duration, and is accompanied by a 1-2 page research summary stating the project objectives, findings and conclusions and by a presentation for MoDOT staff summarising the important or significant details of the project; the final set is delivered 1/1/2026, ahead of the 2/2/2026 contract end. Reports follow the Publication Guidelines and the research summary template published on MoDOT's information-researchers page, and the final report carries a completed Technical Report Documentation page.

component_records.title: Hosting, database, accessibility and security compliance
component_records.description: The drafting application is deployed as a web-based browser application requiring no client-side software beyond a modern browser, with no Java Applets and no Silverlight, on an on-premise database running Oracle 19C. No Personal Identifiable Information is stored in any database table without a specific business need, and any PII that must be stored is submitted to the IS Cyber Security Team for approval before the table is created. All web application screens meet the State of Missouri Accessibility Standard based on Section 508 of the Rehabilitation Act as amended and adhere to WCAG 2.1 at 'AA' level of conformance, verified by automated and manual testing before each release. Content is original or used only where the author explicitly permits free copying or appropriate arrangements are made, and vendor logos and branding are suppressed wherever a supported, licensed option exists to remove them from the display.

component_records.title: Contract, insurance and compliance obligations
component_records.description: We accept the contract provisions specified in the RFP as they will appear in the post-award negotiated contract, and we accept that the award is subject to that negotiation and that MHTC may cancel the award and select a different Offeror if terms cannot be agreed. We will not release any material or report to the public without the prior consent of MHTC's representative, will not assign, delegate or novate any interest in the services without that representative's prior written consent, and accept that any change to the Agreement requires a formal contract amendment signed by authorised representatives of both parties. We remain ultimately responsible and liable to MHTC for the complete, accurate and professional quality and performance of the services regardless of any subcontractor or supplier, we include the Section (3) paragraph I provisions in every subcontract, and we take whatever action with respect to a subcontract the Commission directs as a means of enforcing those provisions, including sanctions for noncompliance. We certify that every employee assigned to the contract is eligible and authorised to work in the United States, and we affirm by sworn affidavit our enrolment and participation in a federal work authorization program such as E-Verify, supply the completed E-Verify Memorandum of Understanding for the employees proposed, and affirm by sworn affidavit that we do not knowingly employ any unauthorised alien in connection with the contracted services; where the entity is a sole proprietorship or partnership, each sole proprietor and general partner provides affirmative proof of lawful presence under Section 208.009, RSMo. The affiant certifies soundness of mind and personal knowledge of the facts stated as required by Section 285.530, RSMo. We do not disclose confidential factual matters provided by MHTC to third parties except as required by statute, ordinance or court order or as authorised by MHTC's representative, and we notify MHTC immediately of any request for such confidential information. All documents, reports, exhibits and materials we produce at MHTC's direction, and information supplied by MHTC, remain MHTC property, and MHTC's representative may reproduce and use derived products without royalties or fees. We maintain all working papers and records and make them available at no charge to MHTC and the Missouri State Auditor at all reasonable times during the Agreement and any extension and for three years from final payment. We carry General Liability of not less than $500,000 per person and $3,000,000 per occurrence, Automobile Liability of not less than $500,000 per person and $3,000,000 per occurrence, and a Missouri State Workmen's Compensation policy or equivalent in accordance with state law, and can provide certificates of insurance prior to contract signing on request. As a further commitment to the RFP's workforce goals we will seek 10% MBE and 5% WBE participation through subcontractors, suppliers or joint ventures and will hire minorities and women directly where we can.

items.text: The Missouri Highways and Transportation Commission (MHTC), acting through the Missouri Department of Transportation (MoDOT), is the client and beneficiary of study TR202504, "Using AI/ML to Write Legal Land Descriptions."
The project is coordinated by the Research Unit of MoDOT's Construction and Materials Division, with Research Director Jen Harper as MHTC's designated representative for administering the agreement.

Property descriptions prepared on MHTC's behalf must follow MoDOT Engineering Policy Guide (EPG) Section 236.4.6.2, using metes and bounds unless a property is acquired in its entirety, in which case the description must be written exactly as it appears on the last deed of record.
Descriptions must recite specific rights when less than fee simple title is conveyed and must be accurately described by metes and bounds, lot calls or 1/4 - 1/4 calls.

Before a general warranty deed, quitclaim deed or similar document is presented to a grantor, a professional land surveyor must review the property description to verify the parcel matches the right-of-way plans and that those plans match the surveyor's gathered survey information.
Writing these legal land descriptions is long and tedious work, which is the pain point driving the study.

MoDOT's fiscal year runs from July 1 to June 30, and quarterly project updates feed the Statewide Planning and Research (SPR) Quarterly Report the Construction and Materials Division submits to FHWA each fiscal quarter.

The goal is to determine the usefulness of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) for producing a "first draft" legal land description (LLD) from MHTC parameters, which MoDOT Right of Way staff would then review and edit.
The Offeror must conduct a thorough literature search and review of other state DOT practices using AI/ML for right-of-way purposes (Task 2).
MoDOT will supply copies of previously approved and filed legal land descriptions to train the machine (Task 3a).
The Offeror must name the program it will use to develop the LLDs before proof-of-concept work begins, and MoDOT Information Systems must approve it before Task 3c can proceed (Task 3b).

The core deliverable is a proof of concept demonstrating how the technology creates draft legal land descriptions on a variety of properties, with MoDOT reviewing the drafts and giving improvement feedback (Task 3c).

Once the system is developed and finalized, the Offeror must train ROW staff and supply a user manual (Task 4), plus a draft Synthesis Report and Research Summary (Task 5) and a final report, 1-2 page research summary, presentation and user manual (Task 6).
The contract period is 15 months, with the project schedule estimated to start November 1, 2024 and the contract ending 2/2/2026 when the final invoice is due.
Proposals are due to MoDOTResearchRFP@modot.mo.gov by August 21, 2024 at 10 a.m. Central, with notification of receipt sent by noon the same day.
Questions and comments must be submitted to MoDOTResearchRFP@modot.mo.gov by 7/17/2024 at 4 p.m. Central, and contacting MoDOT employees by any other method is cause for disqualification.
MoDOT posts its responses to questions publicly on 7/31/2024 and notifies submitters about project selection or interviews on 9/18/2024.

Award goes to the Offeror providing the best proposal, with proposals first checked for responsiveness and then evaluated against criteria established by the Technical Advisory Committee; the RFP does not list those criteria or their weights.

The Offeror must demonstrate at the 4/25/2025 milestone how the AI/ML will create draft LLDs, with MoDOT providing feedback, and after adjustments must create a manual and train ROW staff by 7/25/2025.
An interim presentation is required near the project mid-point (scheduled 9/15/2025) to update MoDOT on progress and direction and to decide whether mid-project corrections are necessary.

The draft final report, summary report and user manual are due 11/3/2025, and the final report, summary report, presentation and user manual are due 1/1/2026, roughly one month before contract end to allow billing to be completed.

The Work Plan is limited to ten (10) pages with font no smaller than 12 points, excluding attached forms and resumes, and must cover all items in Section 2 while recognizing MoDOT's ultimate authority to approve work plans.
Services under the RFP are capped at a not-to-exceed amount of $175,000.

All applications must be built on approved technologies: .NET 6.0 or above (or a currently supported .NET Framework 4.8 or above where specifically needed), with web applications using MVC, Razor Pages or Web API, and approved languages limited to C#, JavaScript, CSS, HTML and Python, where Python is reserved for ESRI scripts and small one-time uses unless large-scale use is approved by the Information Systems Best Practices Review Team (BRPT).

Vendors may not use third-party tools or software that would place a licensing responsibility on MoDOT without prior review and approval by the Information Systems Best Practices Review Team (BRPT) and IS management.

Applications must be web-based browser applications requiring no client-side software beyond a modern browser (no Java Applets, no Silverlight), and on-premise databases must run on Oracle 19C or the latest supported SQL Server, with SQL Server 2016 or higher only if approved by the MoDOT IS Data Service Management team.
No Personal Identifiable Information (PII) may be stored in any database table without a specific business need, and all stored PII must be approved by the IS Cyber Security Team.
All web applications must meet the State of Missouri Accessibility Standard (based on Section 508 of the Rehabilitation Act as amended) and adhere to WCAG 2.1 at 'AA' level of conformance.

All documents, reports and exhibits the Offeror produces at MHTC's direction, and information supplied by MHTC, remain MHTC property, and MHTC may reproduce and use derived products without royalties or fees.

The Offeror must submit a Data Management Plan within 2 weeks after the project kick-off meeting, describing anticipated data/file formats and how platform-independent, non-proprietary formats will be used to ensure maximum future utility of the data.

The Proposal Submission Form, the Price Page template, the Publication Guidelines and the research summary template are referenced only by website link (https://www.modot.org/information-researchers) and are not reproduced in the RFP, so bidders must download them before preparing the proposal.
Proposals are due to MoDOTResearchRFP@modot.mo.gov by August 21, 2024 at 10 a.m. Central, with notification of receipt sent by noon the same day.
Questions and comments must be submitted to MoDOTResearchRFP@modot.mo.gov by 7/17/2024 at 4 p.m. Central, and contacting MoDOT employees by any other method is cause for disqualification.
The study is administered for MHTC by MoDOT's Research Unit in the Construction and Materials Division, with Research Director Jen Harper as MHTC's designated representative.
The contract period is 15 months, with the schedule estimated to start November 1, 2024 and the contract ending 2/2/2026 when the final invoice is due.
Services under the RFP are capped at a not-to-exceed amount of $175,000.
MoDOT will supply copies of previously approved and filed legal land descriptions to train the machine.
The Offeror must name the program it will use to develop the LLDs before proof-of-concept work begins, and MoDOT Information Systems must approve it before Task 3c can proceed.

Property descriptions prepared on MHTC's behalf must follow MoDOT EPG Section 236.4.6.2, using metes and bounds unless a property is acquired in its entirety, in which case the description must be written exactly as it appears on the last deed of record.

Before a general warranty deed, quitclaim deed or similar document is presented to a grantor, a professional land surveyor must review the property description against the right-of-way plans and the surveyor's gathered survey information.

The Offeror must demonstrate at the 4/25/2025 milestone how the AI/ML will create draft LLDs, with MoDOT providing feedback, and after adjustments must create a manual and train ROW staff by 7/25/2025.
An interim presentation is required near the project mid-point, scheduled 9/15/2025, to update MoDOT on progress and direction.
The draft final report, summary report and user manual are due 11/3/2025, and the final report, summary report, presentation and user manual are due 1/1/2026, roughly one month before contract end.

All documents, reports and exhibits the Offeror produces at MHTC's direction, and information supplied by MHTC, remain MHTC property, and MHTC may reproduce and use derived products without royalties or fees.

The proposal is submitted by the 8/21/2024 10 a.m. Central deadline stated in the RFP, and questions are treated as closing at the 7/17/2024 4 p.m. Central cutoff, with all contact through MoDOTResearchRFP@modot.mo.gov only.

The November 1, 2024 start is treated as the planning baseline and the 2/2/2026 contract end as the binding end date, so the schedule is built to the dated milestones rather than to a strict 15-month count.
The $175,000 not-to-exceed amount is assumed to be an all-inclusive ceiling covering every phase, travel, subcontractor cost and the Offeror's fee, with no separate pricing of option years.

The MHTC parameters are assumed to be the parcel, deed, right-of-way plan and rights-to-be-acquired data MoDOT Right of Way staff already assemble for each acquisition, supplied to the engine as structured input fields agreed at kick-off.

The EPG Section 236.4.6.2 rules are assumed to be obtainable from MoDOT's published Engineering Policy Guide at its current edition, and the drafting rules are encoded from that edition and re-verified with MoDOT at kick-off.

The proof of concept is assumed to cover a sample of roughly ten to fifteen properties spanning whole-property acquisitions, partial takings and less-than-fee rights, sized to fit the $175,000 ceiling.

ROW staff training is assumed to be delivered as two remote sessions of up to three hours for up to twenty staff, with recordings and the user manual supplied electronically, and the user manual is assumed to be delivered as a maintained electronic document updated once after MoDOT review.

The literature review is assumed to cover published state DOT research and practice from the last ten years across at least ten states, delivered as a written chapter of the Synthesis Report rather than a standalone memo.

The program named for approval is assumed to be a .NET 6.0 or above application with an Oracle 19C data store, so that MoDOT Information Systems approval is a documentation exercise rather than a technology exception.
The kick-off meeting is assumed to be held within two weeks of contract execution, with MoDOT setting the date, so the Data Management Plan is due within four weeks of contract execution.
The interim presentation is assumed to be delivered virtually at project month ten, consistent with the 9/15/2025 date in the RFP milestone table.
The 11/3/2025 draft date and the 1/1/2026 final date in the milestone table are assumed to govern over the narrative two-month and one-month lead statements.

The Publication Guidelines, research summary template, Proposal Submission Form and Price Page are assumed to be the versions currently posted at https://www.modot.org/information-researchers and are downloaded and followed as issued.

The insurance amounts are treated as binding minimums for pricing purposes, with certificates provided at contract signing, and the E-Verify affidavit and Exhibit B lawful-presence proof are assumed to be provided at contract execution rather than with the proposal.

Confidential factual matters are assumed to be identified by MHTC in writing at the time of supply, and "immediately" is assumed to mean notification within one business day of the Offeror becoming aware of a request.
Oracle 19C is assumed to be the required on-premise database platform, with SQL Server not offered, and the latest IS-approved browsers are assumed to be the current versions of Chrome and Edge.

Exhibit A and Exhibit B affidavits not in the RFP. The RFP requires a sworn E-Verify affidavit (Exhibit A) and, for sole proprietorships and partnerships, a notarised lawful-presence affidavit (Exhibit B), but neither exhibit is included in the document. The bid team cannot confirm the exact wording, notary and SSN/AFID fields, or whether the forms must accompany the proposal or be produced at contract execution; a wrong or late affidavit is a responsiveness failure that can disqualify the bid or stall contract signing. Both exhibits are referenced at page 15 but absent from the PDF, and the requirements impose detailed affidavit content (notarisation, commission expiry, SSN/AFID, citizenship box) that cannot be guessed. The solution's own assumption that these are provided at contract execution rather than with the proposal is unverified.

$175,000 cap against an open-ended scope. The RFP caps total compensation at $175,000 while separately requiring a cost estimate covering all services in the Scope of Work, and it does not say whether the cap includes travel, subcontractor cost and fee or only the offeror's fee. The scope also leaves the number of proof-of-concept properties, training volume and 'accompanying documentation' open, so the fixed ceiling can be consumed before the final report is written. R042 and R091 conflict, and the RFP does not settle what the not-to-exceed amount covers. The solution assumes an all-inclusive ceiling with a ten-to-fifteen property proof of concept, an assumption the RFP does not support.

MoDOT Information Systems approval gates the proof of concept. Task 3c cannot start until MoDOT Information Systems approves the named program, and the RFP does not say what documentation must accompany the name, what criteria apply, or how long approval takes. If approval is slow or the stack draws a licensing or Python question, the 4/25/2025 demonstration milestone and everything sequenced after it slip. R053 makes IS approval a hard gate before proof-of-concept work, and the RFP leaves the approval criteria and turnaround unstated. The solution mitigates by choosing a .NET 6.0/Oracle 19C stack, but that is an assumption about what IS will accept.

EPG Section 236.4.6.2 not supplied and edition unstated. The drafting engine must encode MoDOT Engineering Policy Guide Section 236.4.6.2, but the guide is not included in the RFP and the applicable edition is not stated. If the rules are more detailed than assumed, or the edition changes mid-project, the drafting logic and the surveyor review flag need rework after the demonstration, and the client's legal descriptions may not conform. The guide is a referenced document absent from the PDF, and the RFP does not say whether the bidder must obtain it or which edition governs. The solution assumes the current published edition and re-verification at kick-off, which is an inference.

Proof-of-concept property count and training scope unpriced. The RFP does not state how many properties or which property types the proof-of-concept demonstration must cover, nor the number of training sessions, attendees, duration or delivery mode for ROW staff. The bidder must guess both, and if MoDOT expects a larger sample or on-site repeat training than assumed, the effort grows inside a fixed $175,000 ceiling with no mechanism to recover it. The RFP gives no property count or training parameters, and the solution's assumptions of ten to fifteen properties and two remote sessions of up to three hours for twenty staff are inferences, not RFP facts. Under a not-to-exceed cap the cost lands on the bidder.

MHTC parameters undefined, so the input model is a guess. The engine must turn 'MHTC parameters' into a first draft, but the RFP never defines what those parameters are or in what form MoDOT Right of Way staff supply them. If the real inputs are scanned deeds, plan sheets and free-text notes rather than structured fields, the parsing and data-entry work grows well beyond the assumed design and the demonstration may not reflect how staff actually work. The RFP leaves the parameters undefined, and the solution assumes structured parcel, deed, right-of-way plan and rights-to-be-acquired fields agreed at kick-off. That assumption drives the whole input design and is not supported by the RFP text.

15-month term conflicts with the 2/2/2026 contract end. The RFP states a 15-month contract period but also fixes the final invoice and contract end at 2/2/2026 against an estimated 1 November 2024 start, which is roughly 15 months only on one reading and shorter on another. If the term is enforced as a strict 15-month count from a later execution date, the 1/1/2026 final deliverables and the 2/2/2026 billing window compress, and the bidder carries unbilled effort or a schedule slip. R016 and R041 conflict directly, and the RFP itself calls the November 1, 2024 start an estimate to be finalised during contracting, so the actual term is unsettled. The consequence is a schedule and billing squeeze rather than project failure.

Training corpus quality and supply not guaranteed. The approach depends on MoDOT supplying copies of previously approved and filed legal land descriptions to train the machine, and the RFP does not state how many, in what format, or how consistent they are. If the corpus is small, scanned or inconsistent in style, the model's draft quality at the 4/25/2025 demonstration falls short and the adjustment cycle eats the schedule.
